# Quanto vale a pena pagar no Nintendo Switch 2 na Black Friday 2026

Por Diego Corumba • Editado por Jones Oliveira \| 26/11/2026 às 15:35

Compartilhe:

O **Nintendo Switch 2** foi lançado em 2025 e logo alcançou o topo da lista de desejos da maioria esmagadora dos gamers. O console, além de contar com sucessos como **The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time** e **Pokémon Pokopia**, guarda muito potencial para seus próximos títulos.

Continua após a publicidade

Porém, melhor do que apenas comprá-lo é esperar por uma oferta ou cupom que derrube o seu preço o máximo possível. E **existe oportunidade melhor para ver o valor despencar do que a Black Friday?** A edição de 2026 pode trazer a grande oportunidade para a aquisição do console híbrido.

O videogame da Big N pode ser visto apenas como um upgrade do seu antecessor, mas traz diversos atrativos que chamam a atenção: além dos próprios jogos, temos o comando por **mouse do Joy-Con 2**, **GameChat** e o **microfone embutido**— que reforça seu perfil multiplayer.

Contudo, **quanto vale a pena pagar no Nintendo Switch na Black Friday 2026**? Veja quanto o valor dele pode cair e qual será o melhor momento para garantir o dispositivo mais desejado da indústria dos games:

## O preço sugerido do Switch 2

Como o mercado enfrenta uma grande crise de memórias RAM e armazenamento, ajustes foram apresentados nos valores dos principais videogames do mercado. Com o console híbrido da Big N, não foi diferente: se antes ele era visto por R$ 4.499, **agora seu valor sugerido é de R$ 4.599**.

Não foi um salto expressivo neste ano, mas **ainda assim um peso maior na carteira sempre preocupa** — principalmente quando ele custa um gás de cozinha a mais ou um azeite de oliva extravirgem. Na prática, muitos terão de economizar um pouco mais para garantir o seu neste custo.

Continua após a publicidade

## Promoções em vista

Durante todo o período de 2026, o Nintendo Switch 2 não teve grandes quedas com cupons e ofertas. Ele geralmente pode ser achado por **R$ 4.000** nas lojas, mas abaixo deste preço é muito difícil de ser visto. Quando disponível, ocorre sob condições complexas — como por meio de pagamento PIX, à vista.

No início do ano, ele alcançou o valor mais baixo neste recorte por meio de compra direta em aplicativo com cupom (um combo raro, diga-se de passagem). Deste modo, **o console híbrido podia ser encontrado por volta de R$ 3.500 com um jogo incluso no pacote**, que podia ser Mario Kart World ou Pokémon Legends Z-A.

Se levarmos em consideração que cada título desses custa entre R$ 389,90 e R$ 439,90 separadamente, a promoção se torna ainda mais atrativa — até porque muitos compraram o videogame para jogar um deles. Ainda assim, **não é uma quantia tão acessível quanto foi vista no PS5 no mesmo espaço de tempo**.

Continua após a publicidade

## O que esperar da Black Friday 2026?

Nas próximas semanas, promoções e cupons começarão a aparecer com cada vez mais frequência. Se você busca um Switch 2, possivelmente terá algo em torno do que já foi visto nos últimos meses — com valores em torno de R$ 3.500.

Se você vir o videogame à venda por esse preço ou menor (em lojas confiáveis), vale a pena garantir o seu. Ainda que exista esperança de vê-lo por quantias mais baixas, **a crise de componentes não deixa muita margem para esperar por algo de R$ 3.000 ou menos**.

Continua após a publicidade

A situação se complica com o preço sugerido de seus jogos. Caso você queira jogar o grande lançamento da companhia neste ano, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, terá de desembolsar mais R$ 329,90 (versão digital) ou R$ 439,90 (edição física).

Neste caso, **atente-se bastante a promoções e cupons oferecidos por lojas como KaBuM! e Magazine Luiza** — para que a aquisição dos games não pese diretamente naquilo que você economizou no hardware.

## Vale a pena comprar o Switch 2?

Por fim, você deve se questionar o quanto vale a pena para você comprar o Switch 2 por estes valores. É um excelente videogame, principalmente para quem ama as franquias exclusivas da Nintendo e busca seus grandes sucessos.

Continua após a publicidade

Mesmo assim, é importante que você leve em consideração todos os fatores: recursos, formato híbrido, desempenho e outros que ele apresenta em comparação ao PS5 e XBOX Series. Se obras como **Super Mario Bros, Pokémon, Xenoblade, The Legend of Zelda** e mais não são a sua praia, você pode querer reconsiderar.

Por outro lado, poder levar o seu dispositivo para qualquer lugar e ter os maiores mascotes do mundo dos jogos na palma das mãos ou a um controle de distância, essa vantagem nenhum concorrente supera. Fora a assinatura do **Switch Online**, que permite acesso a um vasto catálogo retrô da história da Big N.

É bom estar atento aos preços do Nintendo Switch 2, mas também pense muito o quanto o videogame tem a agregar neste momento. Se está na expectativa por **Pokémon Ventos & Ondas** em 2027, por exemplo, ele é muito indicado. No entanto, se ficar com **GTA 6** na cabeça, repense o que te atrai nesta plataforma.

A S&P Global Ratings colocou nesta quarta-feira (25) a recomendação de crédito da Nvidia em observação para um possível rebaixamento, afirmando que a saída e a posterior reintegração do presidente-executivo da companhia revelaram pontos fracos na gestão da fabricante de chips e na supervisão do conselho de administração.

“Acreditamos que o longo mandato de certos membros do conselho possa ter comprometido sua independência. As práticas de governança corporativa da empresa também podem não ter acompanhado o rápido crescimento da Nvidia e seu papel como facilitadora tecnológica global essencial”, afirmou a agência de classificação de risco.

A decisão da S&P ocorre em meio a um período turbulento para a liderança da Nvidia. O conselho de administração da empresa reintegrou o presidente-executivo Jensen Huang no início desta semana, dias depois de ele ter renunciado após revelações de casos extraconjugais com subordinadas diretas, bem como com uma empresária chinesa que, segundo a inteligência dos Estados Unidos, seria uma espiã de Pequim.

Críticos e parlamentares norte-americanos se mostraram veementemente contra a reintegração do executivo, questionando a independência do conselho, cujo presidente recém-eleito havia dito aos investidores na semana passada que a Nvidia não recontrataria Huang porque seu comportamento pessoal era incompatível com o código de conduta da empresa.

Ao reintegrar Huang na segunda-feira (23), a Nvidia omitiu qualquer menção aos seus casos extraconjugais, afirmando, em vez disso, que a decisão foi “baseada em informações do governo dos Estados Unidos”, mesmo enquanto um comitê independente do conselho continuava sua investigação sobre denúncias envolvendo ele e uma suposta operação de inteligência estrangeira.

A Reuters informou na quarta-feira (25) que o Departamento de Justiça dos Estados Unidos, não conduziu uma investigação formal sobre Huang antes do presidente norte-americano, Donald Trump, pressionar pelo retorno do executivo à presidência da Nvidia, segundo três fontes a par do assunto.

Em vez disso, o departamento concluiu que não há evidências de que Huang tenha violado qualquer lei com base nas investigações em andamento sobre dois clientes da Nvidia, a Super Micro e a Megaspeed International, suspeitas de contrabandear microchips avançados para a China. Essa conclusão está sujeita a alterações à medida que as investigações continuam.

Atualmente, a Nvidia possui recomendação “AA” da S&P, o que indica grande capacidade da empresa cumprir seus compromissos financeiros. A recomendação mais alta é “AAA”.

A S&P afirmou que poderá cortar a nota da Nvidia nos próximos 90 dias, mas espera que qualquer possível rebaixamento se limite a um nível, a menos que investigações e outras divulgações prejudiquem a reputação da empresa ou suas perspectivas de negócios.

Enquanto isso, a Moody’s afirmou nesta quarta-feira (25) que o retorno de Huang ameniza a incerteza de curto prazo em torno da execução dos negócios da Nvidia e elimina o risco operacional associado à nomeação de um novo líder para a fabricante de chips.

A agência afirmou que a recomendação Aa1 da Nvidia e a perspectiva estável permanecem inalteradas, mas acrescentou que persistem incertezas relacionadas à governança e à regulamentação.

A Nvidia tem desempenhado um papel fundamental no financiamento do setor de inteligência artificial, financiando startups, empresas de computação em nuvem e projetos de data centers, que, por sua vez, gastam grande parte desse capital em chips da própria Nvidia e outros microprocessadores.

Os complexos acordos de financiamento aumentaram a exposição da Nvidia a uma possível desaceleração do setor, afirmam analistas.

Separadamente, o Wall Street Journal noticiou nesta quarta-feira (25) que autoridades norte-americanas não encontraram evidências de que a executiva de tecnologia Alice Huang tenha sido instruída por Pequim a espionar Jensen Huang. O jornal citou fontes a par de uma reunião confidencial.

Autoridades da agência de espionagem dos Estados unidos, CIA; da polícia federal do país, FBI; do Escritório do Diretor de Inteligência Nacional e da Agência de Segurança Nacional (NSA) mantiveram reuniões com comissões de inteligência do Congresso norte-americano e com os líderes parlamentares do país, segundo o jornal.

As autoridades afirmaram que Alice Huang entrou em contato com a agência de espionagem chinesa durante o caso, mas não encontraram indícios de que ela tenha fornecido informações de inteligência significativas, disse o jornal.

A Nvidia e as agências não responderam imediatamente a um pedido da Reuters para comentário. A Reuters não conseguiu verificar a reportagem de forma independente.

A reportagem afirma que as evidências atuais sugerem que Alice Huang e Jensen Huang possam ter tido um relacionamento amoroso, mas que não se tratou de uma ação coordenada pela China, e que novas informações poderiam alterar essa avaliação.

A reunião informativa também observou que Kang Wei, descrito ao “Journal” como marido de Alice Huang por pessoas que os conhecem, era um agente do Ministério de Segurança do Estado da China que mantinha contato frequente com o serviço de inteligência chinês.

# As Anthropic IPOs, Grand Theft Auto VI proves why efficiency isn’t a virtue

Amanda Silberling

8:00 AM PST · November 26, 2026

Share on FacebookShare on XShare on LinkedInShare on RedditShare over EmailCopy Share Link

It should have been impossible for “Grand Theft Auto VI” (GTA VI) to live up to the hype. Fans waited 13 years for the newest installment in the crime-adventure franchise, and Rockstar Games exceeded even those inconceivable expectations when the game finally came out last week.

GTA VI launched as the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic and made $3.79 billion on release day to mark what could be the biggest entertainment event ever – more massive than “Avengers: Endgame” ( $2.9 billion) or Taylor Swift’s Eras tour ( $2 billion).

The 13-year wait certainly fueled the frenzy, and sales, around GTA VI, but some fans craved GTA VI because of what it represents in the emerging era of AI.

Even the biggest workaholics among us – startup founders – scheduled time off to play the game, including Spiry co-founder Dima Beseda, who told TechCrunch, “I reshuffled my workload to free up time around the weekends and even booked vitamin IV drips to keep my energy up.”

Yet some players felt a sense of anticipatory nostalgia as they wiped away a layer of dust on their Xbox to play the game they’d been looking forward to since they were kids.

“We do have a view that GTA is likely to be the last game of its kind to be made this way,” Ben Feder, managing partner at TIRTA Ventures and former CEO of Rockstar parent company Take-Two Interactive, told TechCrunch.

That’s because GTA VI was created entirely without generative AI.

“We’re kind of at this technological moment where this way of developing has sort of reached its natural frontier,” Feder said. “I don’t think you can say that games like this will always be around.”

As millions of people immersed themselves in Vice City, the tech industry witnessed another long-awaited moment: Anthropic became the first major AI lab to go public. At Nasdaq HQ, Anthropic executives gathered to celebrate the Claude maker’s $81.3 billion IPO. At virtually the same moment that Anthropic broke the record for the largest IPO ever, GTA VI was also breaking records with the highest-rated and best-selling game launch of all time.

But when the Anthropic team rang the bell on Thursday, the sound also signaled the end of an era in video game development, and perhaps even in the arts at large.

The AI industry operates with efficiency as its north star. The promise of this technology is that we will be able to automate so much work that we can expand the capabilities of humanity, avoiding needless time spent tinkering with ultimately fruitless ideas. Instead, a prompt goes into an LLM, and a response is spat out.

This technological revolution exploded into the world with some soul-crushing side effects: children are inundated with mind-numbing slop on YouTube, lawyers cite nonexistent cases in court, and tech companies like Meta lay off tens of thousands of people as part of a corporate-branded “ Year of Efficiency.” But against the backdrop of the AI industry’s first major IPO, Rockstar has unveiled a game that about 5,000 people labored over for more than a decade.

The final product is breathtaking, looking so lifelike that it can be hard to distinguish gameplay footage from real life. These sprawling open-world games are usually made possible by procedurally generating new landscapes and objects, but Rockstar has taken the time to painstakingly craft every detail of the world, even developing 30,000 different nonplayable characters with unique appearances and personalities.

The video game industry is already grappling with the threat of AI. Google’s Project Genie, which launched earlier this year, allows users to create and wander around 3D worlds generated from prompts to an LLM. The stock prices of several video game companies faltered around the time of Project Genie’s release, perhaps because of investors’ uncertainty about the future relevance of video game developers.

“The notion that somehow new tools would allow an individual to push a button and generate a hit, market a hit, and bring it to many millions of consumers around the world, it’s a laughable notion,” Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick said at the time. “It’s just never been the case with entertainment.”

Zelnick’s fellow tech CEOs see different future, though. On a Meta earnings call this year, CEO Mark Zuckerberg promised that, “soon, you’ll have an AI that understands you and \[can\] even generate great personalized content for you.”

Elon Musk even went as far as proposing that a game like GTA VI could be made with AI.

“You won’t even have to ask,” Musk wrote on X. “AI will figure what video game you’d like best.”

This is the paradox of “ Grandthropic” week. GTA VI is so impressively vast and captivating because its developers could make mistakes, experiment, and rework ideas, even if that meant delaying the game (twice). GTA VI was incubated with the exact inefficiencies that investors hope AI companies like Anthropic can help eradicate.

“Plenty of fantastic art — video games and elsewhere — almost by definition has to be created slowly, and there’s something to having that kind of inefficiency around it,” Feder said. “Creative output requires deletion, right? Getting to kind of a masterpiece oftentimes requires an enormous amount of deletion. And when you’re talking about a game of the kind of complexity we’re talking about, that kind of deletion ends up being very expensive, and it is by definition not efficient.”

GTA VI reeks of its own humanity – every small detail is loaded with intention, but it’s this impressive precision that keeps the world abuzz, triggering the kind of monocultural moment that has become increasingly rare in a media landscape that revolves around highly personalized social media algorithms.

The game forces the player to slow down, which is either frustrating or genius, depending on your sense of humor. People waited more than three presidential terms for the next installment in a high-octane action franchise, only to download a 212 GB behemoth of a game in which your earliest missions involve driving around doing errands and putting up drywall to make your girlfriend happy. Don’t worry — there are still car chases and shootouts — but in a moment when AI feels suffocating, GTA VI is such an artistic achievement that it is reaching audiences that don’t even like violent video games.

The ultimate fantasy of GTA VI is no longer to role-play as a criminal — the fantasy is just taking your time to relish the mundane and explore an expansive world that developers were given the time and space to perfect.

# Anthropic’s Dario Amodei calls accusations of surrendering human control to AI ‘absurd’

Rebecca Bellan

11:44 AM PST · November 25, 2026

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is pushing back against claims that Anthropic believes we should “surrender human free will” to AI systems. In a long X post on Wednesday, Amodei called the suggestion “absurd.”

“We should never sacrifice legitimacy or self-determination at the altar of efficiency or security,” he wrote. This argument against autocracy applies word for word against governance by AI, and I feel equally strongly that turning over governance to AI is a bad idea…No one who had carefully read my writing or my interviews could reasonably conclude that I believe anything different.”

The statement comes after a growing chorus from Anthropic rivals suggesting that human agency could be at risk if AI is developed irresponsibly. Earlier this month, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said he wanted to ensure people continue to have “agency over the future.”

Meta’s chief AI officer Alexandr Wang also wrote in an essay on X that we “should not be okay with a ‘handover’ of society to AI.”

“It is hard to imagine a world where humanity can maintain control over fully unconstrained recursive self-improvement,” Wang wrote. “Now that we are at a point where the scientific and technical problems on capability progress are likely solved, we must not only make progress in the extremely urgent areas of safety, alignment, and security, but we have to start thinking through how we progress thoughtfully.”

But in published essays, Amodei claims he has repeatedly advocated for democratic oversight of AI, saying the technology should strengthen democratic institutions and that humans should retain ultimate decision-making power.

Amodei noted that there’s a difference between surrendering human free will broadly and the idea that “as AI systems advance, they become capable of doing _specific_ tasks in a more automated way.” As examples, he gave AI driving a car, designing a cancer drug, or writing end-to-end software.

Amodei suggested drawing a line at recursive self-improvement (RSI), or AI that can improve itself without human assistance. Many safety experts see RSI as inevitably leading to a loss of human control, a point Amodei implicitly acknowledged, writing, “we may want limits on this process.”

Still, Anthropic is laying the groundwork for RSI by incorporating AI into an increasing share of its own research and development. # GTA VI developers vote against unionization

Workers voted 75 percent against the IWGB recognition agreement.

Workers voted 75 percent against the IWGB recognition agreement.

Dominic Prestonis a news editor with over a decade’s experience in journalism. He previously worked at _Android Police_ and _Tech Advisor_.

Workers at _Grand Theft Auto VI_ developer Rockstar Games won’t unionize, after the vote for a formal recognition agreement failed, with only 25 percent of votes in favor of unionization. The Independent Workers Union of Great Britain (IWGB) said that Rockstar workers in the union will continue organizing even without formal recognition.

Voting ran from November 12th through 26th, covering the launch of _GTA VI_. If successful, the vote would have established a formal framework for collective negotiation with the studio over pay, overtime, bonuses, leave, and pensions, along with a right to consultation over future changes including AI implementation and layoffs. Without it, Rockstar won’t have an obligation to meet union representatives, though workers and union members can still lobby for change informally.

“For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society - this isn’t a sign to retreat, it’s a sign to double down on what we stand for,” IWGB said in a statement sent to _The Verge_. “Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favour of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognise we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. We’re ready to put in the effort to make that happen.”

When Rockstar fired 31 IWGB members last year, the union accused it of “the most blatant and ruthless act of union busting in the history of the games industry.” That case has gone to a UK employment tribunal, with a judgment still pending.

“We are extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we’ve built together and the launch of _Grand Theft Auto VI_,” Rockstar head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe told _Bloomberg News_. “This result reflects our team’s strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong. As we look ahead, we’re excited to build on all we’ve accomplished together.”

# Why GTA VI’s version of Florida feels so real

Virtual city expert Emma Fraser explains what makes Rockstar’s latest open world work.

Andrew Websteris an entertainment editor covering streaming, virtual worlds, and every single Pokémon video game. Andrew joined The Verge in 2012, writing over 4,000 stories.

There are plenty of reasons why _Grand Theft Auto VI_ is so popular: the 13 years of anticipation, the relatable lead characters and romantic storyline, the sheer level of depth. But another major factor is the sense of place. The _GTA_ series is unmatched when it comes to re-creating the feeling of a bustling, real-world city, and _GTA VI_’s fictional rendition of Florida is the studio’s most lifelike setting yet. It has functioning buses and trains, plentiful buildings you can go into and explore, residents you can chat with, and huge areas where you can interact with wildlife far away from the bright lights of the Miami-like Vice City. For Emma Fraser, an assistant professor at UC Berkeley who studies urban ruins and virtual cities, the sense of realism has created a unique sensation while playing.

“There’s something about this particular game that is really discombobulating and distracting in a sense,” she says. “Because you have these moments where you think, ‘I’m in a place, I’m experiencing a location.’ You comprehend intellectually that it’s not real or that it’s at best a representation, but you still have this feeling in your brain and you’ll still dream about being in that place.”

Fraser teaches courses on topics including urban geography and virtual worlds and has written papers exploring topics like “mapping in the digital age” and “the virtual spectacle of the end of the city.” She says she started researching video game cities in part because, despite their influence and reach, they’re an underexplored space in academia. “I’m a geographer, and geographers are obsessed with cities,” she explains. “So much of geography is thinking about: How do we imagine cities? How do we navigate cities? How do we build cities? How do we map cities? And video games have all of that, but they’re not taken that seriously as an academic interest.”

[](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/1a20dbf258053-screenshotUrl.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Image: Rockstar Games via The Verge

Like much of the world, she’s been looking forward to _GTA VI_ for years, particularly because of Rockstar’s on-the-ground approach to research. Before development on the game began, developers from the studio traveled to Florida to get an accurate picture. As _GTA VI_ producer Rob Nelson told me, the starting point for the game was the setting, rather than the story or characters. “We just went around to feel it out,” he said. “Go to the Everglades, go to the Keys, go to the city, as many places as we can, and start thinking about what aspects of the place we want to incorporate.”

While there are plenty of open-world games, many of the most successful — from _Elden Ring_ to _The Witcher_ — are sent in fantastical spaces. _GTA_ stands apart in how its various settings look and feel true to the real world. And Fraser believes that this is one of the key reasons the series has such universal appeal. “You know immediately how to function in a city,” she explains. “You know there’s going to be law enforcement, there are going to be city blocks, there are going to be pedestrians, cars, and buses. It’s this really interesting environment that gives you a lot of possibilities to get a player more immersed in your world, because they already know a lot about a city as a general concept.”

“You can’t hold a whole city in your mind at one time.”

Fraser describes _GTA VI_’s world as having “implied expansiveness.” It’s not a one-to-one re-creation of the real location. There are plenty of things missing; you don’t see schools or daycares, and parking spaces are relatively sparse. But the game gets enough details right to be recognizable. Fraser explains that as long as certain parts of the city look correct — the lighting, the coastline, the decoration of street corners, the major arterial roads — that’s enough to convince people that they’re in something resembling Miami.

“You can’t hold a whole city in your mind at one time,” she says. “Instead it’s these highlights. What \[Rockstar\] do very successfully in the game is those snapshots. They’ve got far more content that is recognizable as Florida or Miami than they’ve been able to fit into previous games. So it’s a much more overwhelming sense of being in that place.” The “implied expansiveness” also comes in the form of dialogue, radio programs, and TV shows that suggest a much bigger world by discussing places and moments that exist outside of the game you can actually explore.

[](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/1a20dbef79438-screenshotUrl.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Image: Rockstar Games via The Verge

This level of verisimilitude — combined with the fact that players can explore the city from multiple perspectives, everything from walking to flying a plane — has led to an experience that Fraser likens to virtual tourism, which can result in all kinds of different playstyles. “Some tourists are going to blow a lot of money on taxis and get to wherever they’re going as fast as they can,” she explains, “and some people just like sitting on a bus or a train and getting to know a place.” Similarly, there are certain players who will just experience the story and play through the main missions, and others who will get lost in side activities like bird watching.

“Some people just like sitting on a bus or a train and getting to know a place”

What’s also notable about _GTA VI_ is how its relationship-focused premise is motivating some players to experience the world in a much less violent way. And that includes how they move through the city. Some people are driving more carefully to avoid killing civilians, while others are exploring spaces while both characters hang out together. “In the first few games, you’re this empty vessel. You’re a criminal, you’re doing criminal things,” says Fraser. “Whereas with _GTA VI_ your motivation and the way you think about your character is really important.”

Now that the game is out and millions of players are venturing through Vice City, Fraser is hoping to use it to research the ways that real and virtual worlds intersect when it comes to how we navigate cities. _GTA VI_ offers a lot of choice in this regard; you can still steal a Lambo and speed through the streets, but you can also hop on a train, put on some headphones, and listen to a podcast while getting where you need to be. “Because this world is so fully furnished, and you have so many options, you might start to import your own real-world practices into the game,” she says.

But at this point, what has struck her most is the attention to detail that separates the universe of _GTA VI_ from its contemporaries. “You can’t just generate a generic city and stick icons in, which is what a lot of games do,” she explains. “You aren’t going to get a sense of a real place if you do it that way.”

stories.summary: This constellation would increase the number of satellites in orbit by roughly 50-fold.

In an extraordinary decision, the Federal Communications Commission on Wednesday granted SpaceX conditional authorization to deploy a constellation of up to 1 million Starmind satellites designed to serve as orbital data centers.

If fully deployed, this constellation would increase the number of satellites in orbit by roughly 50-fold.

“The United States is moving decisively to ensure that this breakthrough technology creates opportunity, drives investment, and delivers lasting benefits for the American people,” FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said in a statement on Wednesday. “This action opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America’s leadership and growth.”

The decision, announced a day before the Thanksgiving holiday in the United States, represents a major regulatory victory for SpaceX and its founder, Elon Musk, who has allied himself with the Trump administration.

## A long deployment runway

This announcement clears a major hurdle to deploying data centers in space, although it does not establish that orbital data centers are technically or economically viable. Nevertheless, the FCC authorization appears designed to give the company wide latitude as it works through these remaining issues.

For example, SpaceX has seven years to deploy a single operational Starmind satellite under the order. SpaceX has until November 2035 to deploy 100,000 operational satellites, and November 2040 for the full constellation. SpaceX, therefore, has a 14-year regulatory runway to deploy the most ambitious industrial project ever approved for spaceflight.

The authorization includes some conditional aspects. SpaceX has proposed operating in six orbits, ranging from 550 km to about 1,000 km. The company sought a waiver from FCC rules to allow satellites above 600 km to be disposed of into “Earth disposal orbits or heliocentric orbits.” That is, instead of burning them up in Earth’s atmosphere, SpaceX wants the flexibility to move retired satellites into other orbits around Earth, or potentially into orbit around the Sun.

The FCC did not grant this waiver request “because SpaceX has not provided sufficient information for the Commission to determine whether its alternative disposal methods are compliant with the Commission’s requirements.” The company will need to obtain a waiver before deploying any Starmind satellites that are not intended to be disposed of via atmospheric reentry.

However, in other ways the FCC appears to have been incredibly lenient with SpaceX. This is particularly the case with environmental concerns raised by numerous parties that commented on SpaceX’s application to the FCC.

## Dismisses environmental concerns

Half a dozen organizations, such as the Secure World Foundation and American Astronomical Society, raised concerns about deploying so many satellites into orbit, citing collision risks, orbital debris, atmospheric pollution from so many satellite reentries, impacts on astronomical observations, and more. The FCC also received approximately 1,500 public comments concerning SpaceX’s application.

Some of these environmental issues, the FCC said, lay beyond the scope of its review. For example, on concerns about the environmental implications of thousands or potentially tens of thousands of rocket launches, the FCC said, “Potential concerns related to the emissions of rocket launches and the subsequent impacts on the human environment as an indirect result of the Starmind system are outside of the Commission’s purview.”

The FCC also rejected calls for further environmental scrutiny of pollution from satellite reentries, including concerns about aluminum oxides and their potential effects on the ozone layer. “Other concerns, including impacts on the atmosphere caused by satellites burning up on re-entry, remain speculative and not supported in the record,” the FCC authorization states.

As part of its decision, the FCC cited a significant policy change adopted in October, when the agency concluded that space-based activities generally fall outside its obligations under the National Environmental Policy Act. The FCC reasoned that as these activities occur beyond US territory, they don’t constitute federal actions requiring environmental review. As a result, the agency declined to conduct a comprehensive environmental assessment of SpaceX’s Starmind constellation.

stories.text: Aprovação de novo projeto de satélites da SpaceX preocupa astrônomos; saiba o porquê A Comissão Federal de Comunicação (FCC), agência reguladora de telecomunicações nos Estados Unidos, acaba de conceder a SpaceX a aprovação para lançar um milhão dos satélites Starmind . Com o “sinal verde”, a empresa de Elon Musk fica liberada para levar os data-centers de inteligência artificial ao espaço. “Esta ação abre uma nova fronteira para a infraestrutura computacional necessária para alimentar a liderança e crescimento dos Estados Unidos”, declarou Brendan Carr, diretor do FCC. “Ao levar a capacidade computacional para além da Terra, a SpaceX e seus muitos concorrentes que trabalham em seus próprios centros de dados orbitais estão atendendo às demandas do momento”, acrescentou. Se tudo correr conforme o planejado, a SpaceX deve lançar a primeira leva dos satélites Starmind no terceiro trimestre do ano que vem . Os novos equipamentos vão ao espaço com o foguete Starship — que, aliás, já lançou mais de 20 da nova geração de satélites Starlink nos últimos testes de voo realizados. O que é a Starmind da SpaceX Para entender melhor a proposta dos Starmind, vale resgatar brevemente os planos da SpaceX, que vem delineando sua estratégia de negócios com foco em inteligência artificial. Atualmente, a empresa de Elon Musk vem mirando o que enxerga como um “mercado de US$ 28,5 trilhões a longo prazo” , enquanto US$ 23 trilhões do total seriam destinados à aplicação de IA no setor corporativo. É aqui que entra a Starmind. Para o bilionário, o espaço é o futuro da inteligência artificial: por lá, dá para captar energia solar livremente, e não há riscos de divergências em solo sobre obras ou instalações de data centers — é daí que vêm os números ambiciosos da empresa. Para comparação, considere que a era espacial começou em 1957; desde então, a humanidade já lançou mais de 28 mil satélites. A maior constelação em funcionamento atualmente é a Starlink , com cerca de 11 mil unidades; segundo a SpaceX, a meta é expandir a próxima geração da constelação para cerca de 100 mil satélites. Por isso, a aprovação foi recebida com receio pela comunidade científica . “Esse projeto teria não apenas consequências profundas para a astronomia, mas também iria fundamentalmente alterar o céu noturno para todas as pessoas no planeta”, observou Andreas Kaufer, diretor geral do Observatório Europeu do Sul. “Essa aprovação destaca a necessidade urgente de mecanismos internacionais capazes de avaliar atividades cujos impactos se estendem bem além de fronteiras nacionais e afetam um bem comum global”.

stories.text: Forbes, a mais conceituada revista de negócios e economia do mundo. Elon Musk planeja presentear cada criança nos Estados Unidos com duas ações da SpaceX, em uma tentativa de conquistar apoio público para seus negócios de satélites e inteligência artificial durante um período de intenso escrutínio público e político sobre o setor de tecnologia. A pessoa mais rica do mundo anunciou a doação de ações, que totaliza cerca de US$18 bilhões, na véspera do Dia de Ação de Graças e poucas horas depois de a SpaceX ter obtido, na quarta-feira (25), a aprovação do país para lançar 1 milhão de satélites destinados a data centers no espaço. Musk busca expandir o papel da SpaceX no setor de IA, mesmo com o rápido crescimento da infraestrutura de computação gerando preocupações sobre seu impacto ambiental e a influência econômica e política dos bilionários do setor de tecnologia. Candidatos do Partido Democrata opositores ao desenvolvimento de data centers estiveram entre os maiores vencedores nas eleições legislativas de meio de mandato dos Estados Unidos deste mês. “A iniciativa claramente ajuda a ampliar a participação do público na história da SpaceX”, disse Chez Anbu, chefe de consultoria patrimonial do OCBC em Cingapura, nesta quinta-feira (26). “Dar às crianças uma participação econômica direta na empresa cria uma narrativa poderosa em torno de uma participação mais ampla nos benefícios da IA e da economia espacial”, acrescentou Anbu. A Comissão Federal de Comunicações dos Estados Unidos (FCC) informou que aprovou a proposta de constelação de satélites da SpaceX para ajudar a atender à demanda em rápido crescimento por computação de IA. Os astrônomos há muito se preocupam com tais desenvolvimentos no espaço, e a Sociedade Astronômica norte-americana disse estar “desanimada e consternada” com a decisão da FCC. A sociedade alertou que a constelação proposta “prejudicaria significativamente décadas de investimento federal em instalações astronômicas” e a capacidade dos astrônomos e do público de apreciar e estudar o céu noturno. O post Elon Musk Promete Duas Ações da SpaceX para Cada Criança dos EUA por Apoio À IA apareceu primeiro em Forbes Brasil .
